bet: Combining tensor-product interactions (sin·sin, cos·cos) with sum/difference harmonics (sin(π(x+y)), cos(π(x−y))) creates a richer 2D basis that can capture both separable and non-separable structure in the hidden function, which pure separable Fourier or pure polynomial bases miss.

A mixed basis combining quadratic polynomial terms with sine/cosine of x and y captures both smooth non-periodic structure and periodic oscillations, giving the BFGS optimizer more flexible parameterization than pure Fourier or pure polynomial bases alone.
